status: research candidate; not used by runtime

observations.fact: Iterates a pointer array from global 0x200b24b0 with signed count at 0x200b24ac, invokes callback(pointer, context), and brackets iteration with BASEPRI and internal scheduler lock/unlock calls.
Assert dump invokes that iterator with dump_task callback 0x0c2032c8; the current-task pointer is read from 0x200b24d4 outside an exception.
When unwinding a task other than the current task, reads a saved-context pointer at task + 188 and uses entries 0, 5, 34 and 35.
The register dump labels saved-context words 34 and 35 as LR and PC, respectively.

The first routine increments a signed halfword at current task + 0x44 outside exception context; the second decrements it, may merge pending tasks and may issue SVC 0 when the count reaches zero. Their firmware assertion strings identify sched_lock.c and sched_unlock.c. This does not by itself prove all CPUs or exception contexts are stopped.

The exception entry saves registers on the selected MSP/PSP stack and calls 0x0c19bb8c with the resulting frame. The dispatcher stores this frame at the task pointer from 0x200b24d0 + 0xbc and later obtains the next task frame from the pointer at 0x200b24d4 + 0xbc. This corroborates frame ownership during this exception path, but not all task states or processors.

A separate synchronous register-capture routine writes LR to both frame + 0x88 and frame + 0x8c; these offsets cannot always be treated as an interrupted PC and LR without knowing how the frame was produced.

The original entry branches to an indexed dispatcher before IN_FLIGHT is incremented inside dispatch. A preempted thread in that interval is not represented by the counter. Callback-site metadata and trampoline are retained with callbacks cleared after detach or a failed publication, including while restoration is pending; their index is not reused in this runtime session. Raw replacements, runtime unloading and threads in an inline prologue still require independent synchronization.

open_questions: Confirm live task table and saved-context ownership for every task state, including newly created or exiting tasks.
Establish whether other processors or unmaskable exception contexts can execute the target code concurrently.
Prove when saved contexts are stable and how the currently running task and nested exceptions are handled.
Check both executable/data aliases, return paths and any indirect callers; validate the check is held throughout code publication and rollback.
Obtain independent emulator or device observations before using this candidate as an execution barrier.
Include suspended PCs in entry thunks and dispatch code before the in-flight increment, and ensure a site index or trampoline is not reused while any old invocation can still reach it.
Account for raw replacements and return addresses held on stacks or in exception frames; a zero callback counter and a scan of only current PCs are not sufficient.
Distinguish exception frames from synchronous register captures and newly initialized contexts before interpreting the saved PC/LR fields.
